title: Document portability rules in memory notes and CLAUDE.md
problem: Even after the portability refactor lands, future Claude sessions have no durable guidance preventing reintroduction of hard-coded paths, interpreter paths, or platform-specific shell idioms. The rules need to live in memory + CLAUDE.md + scribe so they survive across sessions.
description:
This is independent of the portability refactor itself - it captures the rules so future sessions follow them.

Memory updates:
1. New feedback memory feedback_no_absolute_paths.md - rule: never hard-code absolute paths, home dirs, or interpreter paths in hooks/skills/scripts/settings.json. Why: apiary is intended portable; absolute paths silently break on second environment. How to apply: use $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, pathlib.Path(__file__).parent, sys.executable, ~ expansion.
2. New feedback memory feedback_cross_platform_shell.md - rule: subprocess and shell code must work on Windows-bash, macOS, Linux without branching. How to apply: os.devnull not NUL/dev/null literals; pathlib not string paths; list-form subprocess not shell=True; no .exe suffixes.
3. New project memory project_portability_status.md - fact: portability initiative is active, see ticket [Plan 1 ID]. So future sessions don't duplicate analysis or land conflicting changes.
4. Update MEMORY.md index with one-line pointers to the three new files.

Scribe notes:
5. Add a decision note capturing the high-level architecture: apiary will be portable across OSes; project key will be repo-stable not cwd-derived; state lives in ~/.claude/projects/<key>/ with documented bootstrap.
6. Add a reference note listing the canonical portability rules in one place (mirrors memory files but surfaces in 'notes list').

CLAUDE.md updates (global):
7. Add a 'Portability' section: no absolute paths; no hard-coded interpreters; $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR for repo-relative refs; cross-platform shell only; persistent state under ~/.claude/projects/<key>/.
8. Revisit existing '/dev/null not NUL' line and reframe so it doesn't lock the harness conceptually to one OS.

settings.json:
9. Audit only (do not rewrite - that's the portability ticket's job). List every hook command containing an absolute path, append to portability ticket as the concrete attack surface for Phase 1.

Done when: a future session reading MEMORY.md + CLAUDE.md + active notes would refuse to write a new hook with a hard-coded path, and would know the portability ticket exists.
